input.request: Leads from our website, trade shows and partner referrals are tracked in individual spreadsheets and email inboxes, so leads fall through the cracks and managers have no view of the pipeline. We want one place to capture every lead, assign it to a salesperson, set follow-up reminders and report on conversion. The sales team wants every new lead assigned to a rep automatically within five minutes, but the sales director wants to personally review and approve every lead before it is assigned.
input.stakeholders: Sales representatives, sales director, marketing team, partner managers

input.request: Leads from our website, trade shows and partner referrals are tracked in individual spreadsheets and email inboxes, so leads fall through the cracks and managers have no view of the pipeline. We want one place to capture every lead, assign it to a salesperson, set follow-up reminders and report on conversion. The sales team wants every new lead assigned to a rep automatically within five minutes, but the sales director wants to personally review and approve every lead before it is assigned.
input.stakeholders: Sales representatives, sales director, marketing team, partner managers

clarifications.question: The sales team wants leads auto-assigned within five minutes, but the sales director wants to personally review and approve every lead before assignment. Which of these rules governs the process, or under what conditions does each apply?
clarifications.answer: Leads are auto-assigned immediately. The sales director only reviews leads from strategic accounts (over 500 employees), and those must be approved within 4 business hours or they auto-assign.

questions.question: The sales team wants leads auto-assigned within five minutes, but the sales director wants to personally review and approve every lead before assignment. Which of these rules governs the process, or under what conditions does each apply?
questions.rationale: These two stated requirements are contradictory; without resolving them the assignment workflow cannot be designed and either the speed goal or the approval control will be violated.

questions.question: If the sales director must approve every lead, what is the maximum acceptable delay between lead capture and assignment, and what happens to the five-minute goal?
questions.rationale: A manual approval step inherently conflicts with a five-minute SLA; the actual target must be defined to design reminders and escalation logic.

questions.question: What rule determines which salesperson a lead is assigned to (e.g., territory, product line, round-robin, lead source, workload)?
questions.rationale: Without an assignment rule, the system cannot automate distribution, which is a core objective of the request.

questions.question: What data fields must be captured for each lead from each source (website form, trade shows, partner referrals), and which fields are mandatory versus optional?
questions.rationale: Lead capture and reporting depend on a defined data model; without it, forms, validations and conversion reports cannot be built.

questions.question: How will leads from trade shows and partner referrals be entered into the new system — manual entry, file upload, a dedicated form, or an integration?
questions.rationale: These sources currently rely on spreadsheets and email; the input does not state how they will be captured going forward, which affects both scope and integration design.

questions.question: Does the website contact form need to integrate automatically with the new system, or will marketing continue to manually transfer leads?
questions.rationale: The request implies the website is a lead source, but does not confirm whether direct integration is required, which significantly affects technical scope.

questions.question: What defines a 'converted' lead for reporting purposes (e.g., qualified opportunity, closed deal, signed contract)?
questions.rationale: Conversion reporting is a named requirement, but without a definition of conversion, the metric cannot be built or validated.

questions.question: What happens if the sales director does not review a lead within a defined time — is there an escalation, auto-assignment fallback, or delegation to another approver?
questions.rationale: Without an exception path, leads could stall indefinitely if the director is unavailable, undermining the goal of preventing leads from falling through the cracks.

questions.question: Can the sales director reject or reassign a lead during review, and if so, what happens to a rejected lead (returned to marketing, discarded, flagged for follow-up)?
questions.rationale: The approval step implies a possible rejection outcome, but the resulting workflow is undefined.

questions.question: Who else, besides sales reps, sales director, marketing and partner managers, should have visibility into the pipeline (e.g., executives, finance, customer success)?
questions.rationale: Reporting and pipeline visibility needs may extend beyond the stated stakeholders, affecting access control design.

questions.question: What level of access should marketing team members and partner managers have — can they view lead status/assignment, or only submit leads?
questions.rationale: The system will hold sales pipeline data; without defined access levels per role, authorization rules cannot be specified.

questions.question: Will lead or customer data include personal information subject to privacy regulations, and are there existing data retention or handling policies that apply?
questions.rationale: B2B lead data often includes personal contact details; without clarification, data retention and privacy requirements cannot be defined.

questions.question: How will follow-up reminders be delivered (in-app, email, mobile notification), and who is responsible for acting on overdue reminders?
questions.rationale: Reminders are a named feature, but delivery channel and escalation ownership are undefined, affecting design and adoption.

questions.question: Does the new system need to integrate with any existing tools such as email, calendar, or a CRM, or will it be a standalone system replacing spreadsheets and email entirely?
questions.rationale: The current process uses email and spreadsheets; unclear whether these are fully replaced or need to coexist with the new system.

questions.question: Are there specific timeline, budget, or technology platform constraints (e.g., must use an existing CRM license, cloud-only, mobile access required) that will shape the solution?
questions.rationale: Constraints were marked as not provided; without them, solution options cannot be scoped or prioritized realistically.

questions.question: How will success of this initiative be measured beyond conversion rate (e.g., reduction in lost leads, time-to-first-contact, pipeline visibility for managers)?
questions.rationale: Additional metrics would help validate that the core pain points (leads falling through cracks, lack of pipeline view) are resolved.

questions.question: Should historical leads currently sitting in spreadsheets and email inboxes be migrated into the new system, and if so, how far back?
questions.rationale: Migration scope affects data cleanup effort and reporting completeness but does not block core functional design.

problem.problem_statement: Leads generated from the website, trade shows and partner referrals are tracked manually across individual spreadsheets and email inboxes, causing leads to be lost or delayed and leaving sales management without visibility into the overall pipeline.

objectives.description: Centralize capture of all leads from website, trade show and partner referral sources into a single system so no lead is lost or overlooked.
Automatically assign standard (non-strategic) leads to a sales representative within five minutes of capture.
objectives.success_measure: Lead assigned within 5 minutes of capture

objectives.description: Route leads from strategic accounts (organizations with more than 500 employees) to the sales director for review and approval, auto-assigning them if not approved within 4 business hours.
objectives.success_measure: Strategic account leads reviewed or auto-assigned within 4 business hours

objectives.description: Give sales managers and the sales director real-time visibility into the full sales pipeline.
Enable reporting on lead conversion rates to support sales performance analysis.

problem.current_state: Leads from the website, trade shows and partner referrals are recorded in separate spreadsheets and email inboxes maintained individually, with no shared system, assignment process, or reporting mechanism. This leads to leads being missed and gives managers no consolidated view of the pipeline.
problem.future_state: All leads are captured in a single system regardless of source. Standard leads are automatically assigned to a sales representative within five minutes. Leads from strategic accounts (over 500 employees) are routed to the sales director for approval, auto-assigning after 4 business hours if not reviewed. Follow-up reminders are set for assigned leads, and conversion is tracked and reportable.
in_scope: Capturing leads from the website, trade shows and partner referrals into one system
Automatic assignment of standard leads to sales representatives within five minutes
Conditional approval workflow for strategic account leads (>500 employees) with a 4-business-hour review window and auto-assignment fallback
Setting follow-up reminders for assigned leads
ambiguities: How leads from trade shows will be entered into the system (manual entry, batch upload, or integration) is not specified.
The logic for determining which specific salesperson a lead is assigned to (e.g., territory, round robin, product line) is not defined.
Whether 'strategic account' criteria include factors beyond employee count (e.g., revenue, industry) is unclear.
It is unclear whether the 4-business-hour review clock starts at lead capture or at some other point (e.g., when routed to the director).

stakeholders.name: Sales Representatives
stakeholders.interest: Wants leads assigned automatically and quickly (within five minutes) so they can act on them promptly and not lose deals to delay.

stakeholders.name: Sales Director
stakeholders.interest: Wants visibility into the full pipeline, conversion reporting, and the ability to personally review and approve leads from strategic accounts before assignment.

stakeholders.name: Marketing Team
stakeholders.interest: Generates leads via the website and needs assurance that leads they source are captured accurately and can be tracked through to conversion for campaign ROI reporting.

stakeholders.name: Partner Managers
stakeholders.interest: Needs referred leads from partners to be captured reliably and wants visibility into how partner-sourced leads are progressing and converting.

stakeholders.name: Sales Managers
stakeholders.interest: Needs a consolidated view of the pipeline across all reps to monitor workload distribution and follow-up activity, since current spreadsheets/inboxes give no such visibility.

stakeholders.name: IT / Systems Owner
stakeholders.interest: Responsible for implementing, integrating (e.g., website contact form, email) and maintaining the new lead management system, and for decommissioning or migrating data from spreadsheets and inboxes.

stakeholders.name: Data Privacy / Compliance Officer
stakeholders.interest: Needs to ensure that centralized storage of lead contact data (from website, trade shows, partners) complies with applicable data protection obligations, since data will move from scattered spreadsheets/email into one shared system.

stakeholders.name: Business Process / Product Owner
stakeholders.interest: Owns approval of final requirements, prioritization decisions (e.g., resolving the auto-assign vs. director-review conflict), and sign-off on scope for the new system.

current_state.description: Captures lead information submitted by prospect
Records website lead details into a spreadsheet
Collects lead information at trade show (e.g., business card or notes)
Enters trade show lead into a spreadsheet
Emails partner referral lead details to sales team
Checks email inbox for partner referral leads
Reviews spreadsheets and email inboxes to identify unassigned leads
Manually assigns lead to a sales representative via email
Sets a follow-up reminder manually using personal calendar or notes
Compiles conversion data manually from spreadsheets for reporting

future_state.description: Captures lead from website form, trade show entry, or partner referral
Evaluates lead against strategic account criteria (over 500 employees)
Auto-assigns standard lead to a sales representative within 5 minutes
Routes strategic account lead to sales director for review
Reviews and approves strategic lead within 4 business hours
Auto-assigns strategic lead to a sales representative if not approved within 4 business hours
Sets follow-up reminder for assigned lead
Follows up with lead per reminder
Tracks lead status and conversion metrics

bottlenecks: CS-06: Checking email inboxes for partner referral leads delays capture and risks leads being overlooked.
CS-07: Manual review of scattered spreadsheets and emails to find unassigned leads delays assignment and increases risk of leads falling through the cracks.
CS-08: Manual, email-based lead assignment is slow and inconsistent, undermining the sales team's desire for near-immediate assignment.
CS-10: Manual compilation of conversion data from spreadsheets delays reporting and pipeline visibility.

FS-05: Sales director review of strategic account leads could still delay assignment if the director does not act within the 4-business-hour window, though the system's auto-assign fallback limits the impact.
manual_activities: CS-02: Marketing team records website lead details into a spreadsheet.
CS-03: Sales representative collects trade show lead information manually.
CS-04: Sales representative enters trade show lead into a spreadsheet.
CS-05: Partner manager emails partner referral lead details to sales team.
CS-06: Sales representative checks email inbox for partner referral leads.
CS-07: Sales manager reviews spreadsheets and emails to identify unassigned leads.
CS-08: Sales manager manually assigns lead via email.
CS-09: Sales representative manually sets follow-up reminders.
CS-10: Sales manager manually compiles conversion data for reporting.
FS-05: Sales director manually reviews and approves strategic account leads.
FS-08: Sales representative manually follows up with the lead.
inefficiencies: Leads from three different sources (website, trade show, partner referral) are captured in disconnected spreadsheets and email inboxes with no single source of truth (CS-01 through CS-06).
No automated assignment logic exists, so leads wait for a manager to notice and assign them, contradicting the sales team's expectation of near-immediate assignment (CS-07, CS-08).
Follow-up reminders are set manually and informally, making them easy to forget or lose (CS-09).

Conversion reporting depends on manually compiling data from multiple spreadsheets, delaying visibility into pipeline performance and making the sales director's oversight of the process reactive rather than proactive (CS-10).
automation_opportunities: Replace manual spreadsheet entry for website and trade show leads (CS-02, CS-04) with direct system capture (FS-01), eliminating transcription effort and reducing missed or duplicate leads.
Automate lead routing and assignment (replacing CS-07 and CS-08 with FS-02/FS-03) so standard leads are assigned within 5 minutes without manager intervention.

Automate detection of strategic accounts and routing to the sales director (FS-02, FS-04) with a system-enforced 4-business-hour approval window and auto-assignment fallback (FS-06), preserving director oversight for high-value leads while preventing indefinite delay.
Automate follow-up reminder creation tied to lead assignment (FS-07) so reminders are never dependent on a rep remembering to set them, unlike the manual step in CS-09.

Replace manual spreadsheet-based conversion reporting (CS-10) with system-generated tracking (FS-09), giving managers real-time pipeline and conversion visibility instead of periodic manual compilation.
process.notes: The future-state map assumes a single system can ingest leads from all three sources (website, trade show, partner referral); the exact mechanism for trade show and partner-referral capture (manual entry, batch upload, or integration) is not specified in the input and should be confirmed with stakeholders. The classification of 'strategic account' is assumed to rely solely on employee count (>500) as stated; any additional criteria would need confirmation.

risks.description: Trade show and partner referral leads may require manual entry or batch upload (no integration defined), so leads captured on paper or via partner email are delayed or never logged, missing the 5-minute assignment goal.
risks.mitigation: Define and build a lead intake method (dedicated form or lightweight integration) for trade show and partner leads before go-live, and set an SLA for manual entry timing.

risks.description: The website contact form may not be automatically integrated with the new system, so leads sit in an inbox awaiting manual transfer, undermining the 5-minute auto-assignment commitment.
risks.mitigation: Confirm integration requirement with marketing and IT early; if manual transfer is required, set a maximum handling time and monitor compliance.

risks.description: Strategic account classification depends on employee count data that may be missing, self-reported, or unverified at the moment a lead is captured, causing leads to be misrouted (a large account auto-assigned, or a small account unnecessarily sent to the director).
risks.mitigation: Define a reliable data source for employee count (e.g., enrichment service or mandatory field) and a fallback rule for when it is unknown.

risks.description: A lead could be approved by the sales director at nearly the same moment the 4-business-hour auto-assignment fallback fires, resulting in the lead being assigned twice or to conflicting reps.
risks.mitigation: Implement a locking mechanism so approval and auto-assignment cannot both execute on the same lead, with the earlier action taking precedence.

risks.description: Leads from the same company or contact may be submitted through multiple channels (website, trade show, partner referral), creating duplicate records that split conversion reporting and cause multiple reps to contact the same prospect.
risks.mitigation: Introduce a duplicate-detection rule (e.g., match on email/company domain) and a merge or flagging process before assignment.

risks.description: Sales representatives, accustomed to selecting leads manually from spreadsheets, may resist automatic assignment, leading to leads being ignored or reassigned informally outside the system.
risks.mitigation: Involve sales reps in defining assignment rules, communicate the rationale, and monitor early usage for workaround behavior.

risks.description: Because 'converted' is not yet defined, conversion reports could be built on an ad hoc or inconsistent definition, producing metrics the sales director does not trust or cannot act on.
risks.mitigation: Agree a precise, documented definition of lead conversion with the sales director before reporting requirements are finalized.

risks.description: If lead or contact data includes personal information and no data handling or retention policy is defined, the system could be built without necessary privacy controls, creating compliance exposure later.
risks.mitigation: Confirm with compliance/legal whether personal data rules apply and incorporate any required consent, storage or retention controls into design.

risks.description: Without a defined territory, product-line, or round-robin assignment rule, development of the auto-assignment feature could stall or be built on an incorrect assumption, delaying delivery.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize resolving the assignment logic with the sales director and reps in an early requirements workshop before design begins.

assumptions.description: Leads will be assigned to a specific salesperson using a rule such as territory, round-robin, or workload balancing, to be defined during requirements.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Assignment logic would need to be redesigned, potentially delaying the 5-minute auto-assignment feature.

assumptions.description: Trade show and partner referral leads will be entered into the system manually or via file upload rather than through a real-time integration.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Additional integration work would be required, affecting timeline and the ability to meet the 5-minute assignment target for these sources.

assumptions.description: The existing website contact form will be integrated so leads flow into the new system automatically rather than requiring manual transfer.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A manual handoff step would need to be designed, adding delay risk to the 5-minute goal for website leads.

assumptions.description: Employee count data needed to identify strategic accounts (over 500 employees) will be reliably available at the point a lead is captured.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Strategic leads could be missed or standard leads incorrectly routed to the director, undermining the approval workflow.

assumptions.description: A 'converted' lead will be defined as a signed contract or closed deal for the purposes of conversion reporting.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Conversion reports would measure the wrong outcome and require rebuilding once the correct definition is confirmed.

assumptions.description: The new system will operate as a standalone tool and does not need to integrate with an existing CRM, calendar, or email system.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Additional integration requirements would need to be scoped, affecting technical design and timeline.

assumptions.description: The 4-business-hour review window for strategic account leads starts at the moment the lead is captured, not at a later routing step.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The auto-assignment fallback timing logic would need to be redefined, changing when strategic leads default to auto-assignment.

assumptions.description: Marketing team members and partner managers will have permission to submit leads and view basic status, but not full pipeline or reporting access.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Access control design and reporting views would need to be revised to reflect broader or narrower permissions.

assumptions.description: No specific budget, deadline, or mandated technology platform has been set for this project.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Solution options and delivery timeline would need to be re-evaluated against any newly disclosed constraint.

assumptions.description: Lead and contact data collected does not currently fall under a defined privacy or retention policy beyond general good practice.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Additional compliance controls (consent capture, retention limits, data handling) would need to be added to the design.

constraints.description: The solution must accommodate leads originating from three existing channels: the website contact form, trade shows, and partner referrals, which are currently tracked in spreadsheets and email.
Standard (non-strategic) leads must be automatically assigned to a sales representative within five minutes of capture.
Leads from accounts with more than 500 employees must be routed to the sales director for review, with a 4-business-hour approval window before auto-assignment occurs.
The strategic account threshold is defined by employee count exceeding 500; no other qualifying criteria have been specified.

edge_cases: A lead is captured without employee count data available, making it impossible to determine whether it qualifies as a strategic account.
A lead from a strategic account is submitted near the end of business hours, so the 4-business-hour review window spans a weekend, holiday, or overnight period.
The same contact or company submits leads through more than one channel (e.g., website and trade show) within a short time, creating duplicate lead records.
The sales director approves or rejects a strategic lead at nearly the same moment the 4-hour auto-assignment fallback is triggered, risking a double or conflicting assignment.
A partner referral or trade show lead is entered with incomplete contact information (e.g., missing email or phone number), preventing follow-up or assignment.

A company's employee count changes (e.g., due to a data update or acquisition) between when a lead is first captured and when it would be classified, changing whether it should have been routed to the director.
A lead is assigned to a sales representative who is unavailable, on leave, or has left the company at the time of assignment.
A trade show batch upload contains malformed, incomplete, or duplicate records that fail standard field validation.
A lead rejected or declined by the sales director needs a defined next step, such as returning to marketing, discarding, or flagging for later follow-up.

functional.description: The system shall capture lead information submitted through the website contact form into a single lead record.
functional.rationale: Leads from the website are currently tracked separately in spreadsheets, causing loss and delay; centralizing capture is core to the objective of a single lead repository.

functional.description: The system shall allow authorized users to manually enter lead information collected at trade shows.
functional.rationale: Trade show leads are currently recorded informally (business cards, notes) and must reach the central system; the capture mechanism is not fully specified so manual entry is assumed as the baseline method.

functional.description: The system shall allow partner managers to submit partner referral lead information directly into the system.
functional.rationale: Partner referrals are currently emailed and checked manually, a known bottleneck; direct submission removes reliance on email inboxes.

functional.description: The system shall require a minimum set of contact fields (such as name and email or phone) before a lead record can be saved, and shall reject submissions missing these fields with an explanatory error.
functional.rationale: Incomplete lead records prevent follow-up and assignment, undermining pipeline reliability.

functional.description: The system shall evaluate each captured lead against the strategic account criterion of more than 500 employees to classify it as standard or strategic.
functional.rationale: This classification determines whether a lead is auto-assigned or routed for director review, per the agreed process.

functional.description: The system shall automatically assign each standard (non-strategic) lead to a sales representative within five minutes of capture.
functional.rationale: Directly fulfills the sales team's requirement for near-immediate assignment and removes the manual assignment bottleneck.

functional.description: The system shall route each strategic account lead (over 500 employees) to the sales director for review and approval instead of auto-assigning it immediately.
functional.rationale: Preserves the sales director's requirement to personally review high-value leads before assignment.

functional.description: The system shall allow the sales director to approve a strategic account lead and assign it to a specific sales representative.
functional.rationale: Enables the director to exercise the review authority defined for strategic accounts.

functional.description: The system shall automatically assign a strategic account lead to a sales representative if the sales director has not approved it within 4 business hours of routing.
functional.rationale: Prevents strategic leads from stalling indefinitely if the director does not act in time, balancing oversight with responsiveness.

functional.description: The system shall prevent a strategic account lead from being assigned more than once when a director approval and the 4-business-hour auto-assignment fallback occur close together, giving precedence to whichever action completes first.
functional.rationale: Avoids conflicting or duplicate assignment of the same lead to different representatives, a risk identified in the approval/fallback timing overlap.

functional.description: The system shall automatically create a follow-up reminder for a sales representative when a lead is assigned to them.
functional.rationale: Removes reliance on reps remembering to set reminders manually, addressing a current source of missed follow-up.

functional.description: The system shall notify a sales representative when a new lead has been assigned to them.
functional.rationale: Ensures reps become aware of new leads promptly enough to act within the intended assignment window.

functional.description: The system shall provide sales managers and the sales director with a consolidated view of all leads and their current status across the pipeline.
functional.rationale: Directly addresses the lack of pipeline visibility that is a stated business problem.

functional.description: The system shall generate reports on lead conversion across sources and sales representatives.
functional.rationale: Supports sales performance analysis and reporting need stated by the business.

functional.description: The system shall flag potential duplicate leads when a matching contact or company is captured through more than one channel within a short period.
functional.rationale: Prevents duplicate reps contacting the same prospect and split conversion reporting, a risk identified from leads entering via multiple channels.

functional.description: The system shall not integrate with any external CRM, calendar, or email system in this release.
functional.rationale: Recorded scope boundary since no integration requirement with existing tools beyond the website form has been confirmed by stakeholders.

functional.description: The system shall not automatically enrich lead records with third-party employee count or firmographic data in this release.
functional.rationale: No data enrichment source has been specified or confirmed; strategic account classification will rely on data provided at capture until this is resolved.

non_functional.description: The system shall complete automatic assignment of a standard lead within the target time window from the moment the lead is captured.
non_functional.rationale: Meeting the five-minute assignment expectation is a core, explicitly stated success factor for the sales team.
non_functional.measurable_target: Assignment completed within 5 minutes of capture

non_functional.description: The system shall reliably capture and retain every submitted lead without loss, regardless of source.
non_functional.rationale: The central business problem is leads falling through the cracks; the new system must eliminate that failure mode.

non_functional.description: The system shall restrict access to lead data and assignment/approval actions based on the user's role (sales representative, sales director, marketing, partner manager).
non_functional.rationale: Different stakeholder groups have different needs and should not have unrestricted access to pipeline data or approval controls, particularly the director-only approval step.

non_functional.description: The system shall handle lead contact data (such as names, emails and phone numbers) in a manner consistent with applicable data protection obligations, to be confirmed with compliance stakeholders.
non_functional.rationale: Centralizing personal contact data from multiple sources into one system increases exposure if handling requirements are not defined and applied.

non_functional.description: The system shall allow sales representatives and partner managers to enter or review lead information with minimal steps, suitable for use in time-constrained settings such as a trade show floor.
non_functional.rationale: Manual entry of trade show leads must be quick and simple to encourage adoption and avoid a return to informal note-taking.

non_functional.description: The system shall be available during normal business hours so that lead capture, assignment and the director's review window function without interruption.
non_functional.rationale: The 4-business-hour approval window and 5-minute assignment target both depend on the system being consistently operational during working hours.

use_cases.name: Capture New Lead
use_cases.primary_actor: Lead source (Website Visitor, Sales Representative, or Partner Manager)
use_cases.goal: Get a new lead recorded as a single record in the system, regardless of which channel it came from, so it can be classified and routed for assignment.
preconditions: The lead source has access to the applicable capture method (public website form, internal lead entry screen, or partner submission screen).
main_flow: Website visitor completes and submits the website contact form.
System captures the submitted information into a new lead record.
System validates that the required contact fields (such as name and email or phone) are present.
System evaluates the lead against the strategic account criterion (more than 500 employees).
System classifies the lead as standard or strategic.
System routes the lead to auto-assignment (if standard) or to the sales director's review queue (if strategic).
System confirms successful capture to the website visitor.

alternative_flows.name: 1a. Sales Representative enters a trade show lead
steps: Sales representative opens the lead entry screen.
Sales representative manually enters the lead's contact information collected at the trade show.
Sales representative submits the lead.
System proceeds with validation as in main flow step 3.

alternative_flows.name: 1b. Partner Manager submits a partner referral lead
steps: Partner manager opens the partner referral submission screen.
Partner manager enters the referred lead's information.
Partner manager submits the lead.
System proceeds with validation as in main flow step 3.

exceptions.name: 3a. Required contact fields are missing
steps: System detects that required contact fields are missing from the submission.
System rejects the submission and displays an explanatory error.
Lead source corrects the missing information and resubmits.

exceptions.name: 4a. Potential duplicate lead detected
steps: System detects a matching contact or company already captured through another channel within a short period.
System flags the new lead record as a potential duplicate.
System proceeds with classification and routing while marking the record for review.

postconditions: A new lead record exists in the system with validated contact information.
The lead has been classified as standard or strategic.
The lead is queued for either automatic assignment or director review.

use_cases.name: Auto-Assign Standard Lead and Notify Representative
use_cases.goal: Assign a standard (non-strategic) lead to a sales representative within five minutes of capture and ensure follow-up is scheduled.
preconditions: A lead has been captured and classified as standard.
main_flow: System detects a newly captured lead classified as standard.
System selects an available sales representative according to assignment rules.
System assigns the lead to the selected sales representative within five minutes of capture.
System creates a follow-up reminder for the sales representative.
System notifies the sales representative that a new lead has been assigned.
Sales representative reviews the assigned lead's details.
postconditions: The standard lead is assigned to a sales representative.
A follow-up reminder exists for the assigned representative.
The representative has been notified of the new assignment.

use_cases.name: Review and Approve Strategic Account Lead
use_cases.goal: Personally review and approve leads from strategic accounts before they are assigned to a sales representative.
preconditions: A lead has been captured and classified as strategic (more than 500 employees).
The lead has been routed to the sales director's review queue.
main_flow: System routes the strategic lead to the sales director's review queue.
Sales director reviews the lead's details.
Sales director selects a sales representative and approves the lead for assignment.
System assigns the lead to the selected sales representative.
System creates a follow-up reminder for the assigned representative.
System notifies the sales representative that a new lead has been assigned.

exceptions.name: 2a. Sales director does not act within 4 business hours
steps: The 4-business-hour review window elapses without director action.
System automatically assigns the lead to a sales representative.
System creates a follow-up reminder for the assigned representative.
System notifies the sales representative that a new lead has been assigned.

exceptions.name: 3a. Director approval and automatic fallback assignment occur concurrently
steps: Sales director submits approval at nearly the same time the 4-business-hour window elapses.
System detects that both the manual approval and the automatic fallback are attempting to assign the lead.
System honors whichever assignment action completes first and disregards the other.
System prevents the lead from being assigned more than once.

postconditions: The strategic lead has been assigned to exactly one sales representative, either by director approval or automatic fallback.
A follow-up reminder exists for the assigned representative.

use_cases.name: View Pipeline and Generate Conversion Reports
use_cases.goal: View a consolidated view of the lead pipeline and generate conversion reports across sources and sales representatives.
preconditions: The sales director has access to the reporting view.
Leads exist in the system.
main_flow: Sales director opens the pipeline view.
System displays a consolidated list of all leads and their current status.
Sales director requests a conversion report, optionally filtered by source or sales representative.
System generates the conversion report based on the selected filters.
Sales director reviews the report to assess pipeline and sales performance.

alternative_flows.name: 3a. Sales director requests a report without filters
steps: Sales director requests a conversion report covering all sources and representatives.
System generates the report across the entire pipeline.

postconditions: The sales director has current visibility into pipeline status and conversion performance.

criteria.title: Website form lead captured successfully
criteria.given: a visitor completes the website contact form with all required contact fields
criteria.when: the form is submitted
criteria.then: a new lead record is created in the central lead management system with the submitted information, without requiring any manual re-entry

criteria.title: Website form submitted with missing required fields
criteria.given: a visitor completes the website contact form but omits a required contact field such as email or phone
criteria.when: the form is submitted
criteria.then: the system does not create an incomplete lead record and an explanatory error indicates the missing information is required

criteria.title: Same contact submitted through website and another channel
criteria.given: a contact or company already exists as a lead captured through another channel within a short period
criteria.when: a matching lead is submitted through the website contact form
criteria.then: the system flags the new website submission as a potential duplicate for review rather than silently creating a separate untracked record

criteria.title: Trade show lead entered with all required fields
criteria.given: a sales representative is entering a lead collected at a trade show and provides all required contact fields
criteria.when: the representative saves the lead record
criteria.then: the lead record is saved into the central lead management system and becomes available for assignment and follow-up

criteria.title: Trade show lead missing required contact information
criteria.given: a sales representative is entering a trade show lead and leaves a required contact field, such as email or phone, blank
criteria.when: the representative attempts to save the lead record
criteria.then: the system prevents the record from being saved and displays an explanatory error identifying the missing required field

criteria.title: Lead saved with an alternative required contact method
criteria.given: a sales representative enters a trade show lead with a name and a phone number but no email address
criteria.when: the representative saves the lead record
criteria.then: the system accepts and saves the lead record because the minimum required contact information has been satisfied

criteria.title: Batch of trade show leads contains malformed or duplicate entries
criteria.given: a sales representative is entering multiple trade show leads and one or more entries are incomplete, malformed, or duplicate against existing records
criteria.when: the representative attempts to save the batch of leads
criteria.then: the system saves the valid entries, rejects the invalid or duplicate entries individually, and identifies which entries require correction

criteria.title: Successful partner referral submission
criteria.given: a partner manager is logged in and has a complete set of contact details for a referred lead
criteria.when: the partner manager submits the lead information directly into the system
criteria.then: the lead record is created and visible in the system for tracking, without any email exchange required

criteria.title: Partner referral missing required contact information
criteria.given: a partner manager is entering a referral lead but has not provided a required contact field such as email or phone
criteria.when: the partner manager attempts to submit the lead
criteria.then: the system rejects the submission and displays an error explaining that required contact information is missing

criteria.title: Partner referral matches an existing lead from another channel
criteria.given: a contact or company already has a lead record captured through another channel such as the website
criteria.when: a partner manager submits a referral for the same contact or company
criteria.then: the system flags the new submission as a potential duplicate so it can be reviewed rather than treated as an entirely separate lead

criteria.title: Lead automatically classified as strategic
criteria.given: a lead has been captured with an employee count greater than 500
criteria.when: the system evaluates the lead against the strategic account criterion
criteria.then: the lead is classified as strategic and routed to the sales director for review instead of being auto-assigned

criteria.title: Lead automatically classified as standard
criteria.given: a lead has been captured with an employee count of 500 or fewer
criteria.when: the system evaluates the lead against the strategic account criterion
criteria.then: the lead is classified as standard and proceeds to automatic assignment rather than director review

criteria.title: Lead captured without employee count data
criteria.given: a lead has been captured but no employee count value is available for the associated company
criteria.when: the system attempts to classify the lead as standard or strategic
criteria.then: the system records that classification could not be determined and the lead is identifiable for follow-up rather than being silently treated as standard

criteria.title: Employee count changes after initial classification
criteria.given: a lead was classified based on an employee count that is later updated, changing whether it exceeds the strategic threshold
criteria.when: the updated employee count becomes available in the system
criteria.then: the discrepancy between the original classification and the updated criterion is visible so a sales director can review whether the lead's routing was appropriate

criteria.title: Standard lead auto-assigned within five minutes
criteria.given: a new lead has been captured and classified as a standard (non-strategic) account
criteria.when: the lead capture and classification are completed
criteria.then: the system automatically assigns the lead to a sales representative within five minutes of capture and creates a follow-up reminder for that representative

criteria.title: Lead submission missing required contact field
criteria.given: a lead is being submitted through the website form, a trade show entry, or a partner referral without a required contact field such as name, email, or phone number
criteria.when: a user attempts to save the lead record
criteria.then: the system rejects the submission, displays an explanatory error identifying the missing field, and does not create an assignable lead record

criteria.title: Duplicate lead captured through multiple channels
criteria.given: a lead with a matching contact or company has already been captured through one channel and is then submitted again through another channel within a short period
criteria.when: the second matching lead record is captured
criteria.then: the system flags the new record as a potential duplicate for review in addition to proceeding with standard auto-assignment processing

criteria.title: Director approves strategic lead within review window
criteria.given: a lead has been classified as a strategic account (over 500 employees) and routed to the sales director for review
criteria.when: the sales director approves the lead and selects a sales representative within the 4-business-hour review window
criteria.then: the lead is assigned to the selected representative, a follow-up reminder is created, and the lead is recorded as assigned exactly once

criteria.title: Automatic fallback assignment after director inaction
criteria.given: a strategic account lead has been routed to the sales director for review and 4 business hours have elapsed since routing without director approval
criteria.when: the 4-business-hour review window expires
criteria.then: the system automatically assigns the lead to a sales representative and records the assignment as originating from the fallback rule

criteria.title: Director approval and fallback trigger occur near-simultaneously
criteria.given: a strategic account lead is nearing the end of its 4-business-hour review window and the sales director submits an approval at approximately the same time the automatic fallback assignment would trigger
criteria.when: both the director's approval action and the fallback assignment process attempt to assign the lead
criteria.then: the system assigns the lead to only one representative based on whichever action completes first, and prevents the other action from creating a conflicting or duplicate assignment

criteria.title: Review window spans non-business hours
criteria.given: a strategic account lead is routed to the sales director for review near the end of business hours such that the 4-business-hour window would otherwise extend into evening, overnight, weekend, or holiday time
criteria.when: the system calculates the remaining time in the review window
criteria.then: only business hours are counted toward the 4-hour window, so the deadline for the automatic fallback assignment is extended to account for the intervening non-business time

criteria.title: Automatic reminder and notification for standard lead assignment
criteria.given: a standard (non-strategic) lead has been captured and is eligible for automatic assignment
criteria.when: the system automatically assigns the lead to a sales representative
criteria.then: a follow-up reminder is created for that representative and the representative receives a notification that the lead has been assigned

criteria.title: Reminder and notification for director-approved strategic lead
criteria.given: a strategic account lead has been routed to the sales director for review
criteria.when: the sales director approves the lead and assigns it to a sales representative
criteria.then: a follow-up reminder is created for that representative and the representative receives a notification that the lead has been assigned

criteria.title: Reminder and notification when strategic lead auto-assigns after review window
criteria.given: a strategic account lead has been routed to the sales director and the 4-business-hour review window has elapsed without a decision
criteria.when: the system automatically assigns the lead to a sales representative
criteria.then: a follow-up reminder is created for that representative and the representative receives a notification that the lead has been assigned

criteria.title: Reminder still created when assigned representative is unavailable
criteria.given: a lead is assigned to a sales representative who is on leave or otherwise unavailable at the time of assignment
criteria.when: the assignment is completed
criteria.then: the follow-up reminder and notification are still created and recorded against that representative for action when they become available

criteria.title: Consolidated pipeline view for sales manager
criteria.given: leads have been captured from the website, trade shows and partner referrals and are at various stages of assignment or follow-up
criteria.when: the sales manager opens the consolidated pipeline view
criteria.then: the manager sees all leads with their current status, assigned representative and source in a single view

criteria.title: Leads at risk of stalling are identifiable
criteria.given: one or more leads have remained without follow-up action or assignment for longer than expected
criteria.when: the sales manager views the consolidated pipeline
criteria.then: those leads are visibly distinguishable so the manager can identify them as at risk of stalling

criteria.title: Unauthorized user denied access to consolidated pipeline view
criteria.given: a user without sales manager or sales director role attempts to access the consolidated pipeline view
criteria.when: the user requests the view
criteria.then: the system denies access and the user does not see the consolidated lead data

criteria.title: Consolidated view with no leads in the pipeline
criteria.given: no leads have yet been captured in the system
criteria.when: the sales manager opens the consolidated pipeline view
criteria.then: the view displays an empty pipeline state without errors

criteria.title: Generate conversion report across sources and representatives
criteria.given: the sales director is logged in and lead records with assignment and outcome data exist in the system
criteria.when: the sales director requests a lead conversion report broken down by source and by sales representative
criteria.then: the system displays conversion figures grouped by lead source and by sales representative that reflect the underlying lead records

criteria.title: Report requested for a period with no leads
criteria.given: the sales director selects a reporting period or filter for which no leads were captured
criteria.when: the sales director generates the conversion report
criteria.then: the system displays the report with an indication that no lead data is available for the selected criteria, rather than an error

criteria.title: Non-director role attempts to access conversion reports
criteria.given: a user without sales director or authorized reporting permissions is logged in
criteria.when: that user attempts to access the lead conversion report
criteria.then: the system denies access and does not display the report data

criteria.title: Report includes leads not yet resolved
criteria.given: some leads in the system are still pending assignment or director approval and have not reached a final outcome
criteria.when: the sales director generates the conversion report covering those leads
criteria.then: the report distinguishes leads with a final conversion outcome from leads that are still in progress, without treating unresolved leads as converted or lost

criteria.title: Duplicate lead captured through two channels is flagged
criteria.given: a lead matching the same contact or company has been captured through one channel and is then captured again through a different channel within a short period
criteria.when: the second lead record is captured
criteria.then: the system flags the new record as a potential duplicate and alerts the relevant sales representative

criteria.title: Single-channel lead is not flagged as duplicate
criteria.given: a lead is captured once through a single channel and no matching contact or company has been previously captured
criteria.when: the lead record is saved
criteria.then: the system does not raise a duplicate alert for that lead

criteria.title: Duplicate detected after both leads already assigned to different representatives
criteria.given: two lead records for the same contact or company captured through different channels have already been assigned to two different sales representatives
criteria.when: the system identifies the potential duplicate after both assignments have occurred
criteria.then: the system alerts both affected sales representatives that a potential duplicate exists so the conflict can be resolved

criteria.title: Partial match between leads is treated as uncertain duplicate
criteria.given: two lead records share some matching details, such as the same company but a different individual contact, captured through different channels
criteria.when: the system evaluates the records for duplication
criteria.then: the system flags the records as a potential duplicate for the sales representative to review and confirm, rather than automatically merging or discarding either record

test_cases.scenario: Employee count is updated after a lead was already classified, crossing the strategic threshold

test_cases.scenario: Verify a standard (non-strategic) lead is automatically assigned to a sales representative within five minutes and a follow-up reminder is created.

At least one sales representative is available in the assignment pool

test_cases.scenario: Verify lead submissions missing a required contact field are rejected across all capture channels.

test_cases.scenario: Verify a lead captured through a second channel with a matching contact or company is flagged as a potential duplicate while still proceeding through standard auto-assignment.

test_cases.scenario: Verify the sales director can review, approve, and assign a strategic account lead within the 4-business-hour review window.

The 4-business-hour review window has not yet elapsed
steps: Log in as the sales director and open the pending review queue.
Select lead LEAD-4001, approve it, and choose sales representative REP-Chen for assignment.
Confirm the assignment completes within the 4-business-hour window.
Check REP-Chen's task list for a follow-up reminder.
Verify the lead's assignment history shows a single assignment record.
test_cases.expected_result: Lead LEAD-4001 is assigned to REP-Chen, a follow-up reminder is created for REP-Chen, and the lead is recorded as assigned exactly once.

test_cases.scenario: Verify a strategic account lead is automatically assigned to a sales representative if the sales director takes no action within the 4-business-hour review window.
preconditions: Lead LEAD-4002 for a company with 600 employees (strategic account) has been routed to the sales director for review
No director action has occurred as the 4-business-hour window nears expiry
steps: Allow the 4-business-hour review window for lead LEAD-4002 to fully elapse without director approval.
Monitor the lead's assignment status at the moment the window expires.
Inspect the resulting assignment record's origin field.
test_cases.expected_result: Lead LEAD-4002 is automatically assigned to a sales representative immediately after the 4-business-hour window expires, and the assignment record indicates it originated from the fallback rule.

test_cases.scenario: Verify only a single assignment results when director approval and the automatic fallback assignment are triggered at approximately the same time.
preconditions: Lead LEAD-4003 for a company with 1200 employees (strategic account) is nearing the end of its 4-business-hour review window
The sales director is actively viewing the pending review queue near the deadline
steps: Simulate the sales director submitting approval for lead LEAD-4003 with representative REP-Lopez at approximately the same moment the 4-business-hour window is set to expire.
Trigger the automatic fallback assignment process for lead LEAD-4003 concurrently with the approval action.
Inspect the lead's final assignment record and assigned representative field.
Check for any error or conflict log entries related to duplicate assignment attempts.
test_cases.expected_result: Lead LEAD-4003 is assigned to exactly one sales representative based on whichever action completed first, and the other action is prevented from creating a conflicting or duplicate assignment.

test_cases.scenario: Verify the 4-business-hour review window calculation excludes non-business hours, extending the fallback deadline accordingly.
preconditions: Lead LEAD-4004 for a company with 700 employees (strategic account) is routed to the sales director for review 1 hour before the end of business hours on a business day
The following period includes non-business overnight hours before the next business day begins
steps: Route lead LEAD-4004 to the sales director for review 1 hour before business close.
Allow the clock to pass through the overnight non-business period into the next business day.
Monitor the system's calculated remaining review time and fallback deadline throughout this period.
Confirm the fallback assignment does not trigger during the non-business hours.
test_cases.expected_result: The system counts only business hours toward the 4-hour window, extending the fallback deadline to account for the intervening non-business time, and does not trigger the fallback assignment until the full 4 business hours have actually elapsed within business hours.

test_cases.scenario: Reminder and notification are still created when the assigned representative is unavailable (on leave)

Sales representative Rep-Alex is marked as on leave / unavailable in the system
Rep-Alex is the eligible representative selected by the assignment logic
